segments.source: Overview
segments.normalizedSource: Overview
segments.contextBefore: Highlight a model by adding an outline effect.
segments.contextAfter: Emphasizing the edges of a model with an outline is an effective way to highlight and call attention to it, especially when it’s the target of a person’s gaze or interaction.
segments.documentTitle: Creating a Fresnel outline effect with Shader Graph

segments.source: Emphasizing the edges of a model with an outline is an effective way to highlight and call attention to it, especially when it’s the target of a person’s gaze or interaction.
segments.normalizedSource: Emphasizing the edges of a model with an outline is an effective way to highlight and call attention to it, especially when it’s the target of a person’s gaze or interaction.
segments.contextBefore: Overview
segments.contextAfter: One way to add an outline to a model is to approximate the Fresnel effect, wherein the angle between the view direction and the surface normal of a model affects the shading around its edges.
segments.documentTitle: Creating a Fresnel outline effect with Shader Graph

segments.source: One way to add an outline to a model is to approximate the Fresnel effect, wherein the angle between the view direction and the surface normal of a model affects the shading around its edges.
segments.normalizedSource: One way to add an outline to a model is to approximate the Fresnel effect, wherein the angle between the view direction and the surface normal of a model affects the shading around its edges.
segments.contextBefore: Emphasizing the edges of a model with an outline is an effective way to highlight and call attention to it, especially when it’s the target of a person’s gaze or interaction.
segments.contextAfter: Specifically, you can highlight the edges of a model by taking the dot product between the view direction and the surface normal direction and applying an emissive color to the areas where the dot product is close to zero (that is, the vectors are perpendicular).
